newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-VSE seen best for high profile Australians.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-VSE seen best for high profile Australians.

text.p: Australian companies listing on the Vancouver Stock Exchange (VSE) needed to develop a high profile to enjoy the benefits of listing, a newly appointed VSE board member said on Monday.
Larry McFadden, also a senior vice president at Vancouver broker Wolverton Securities Ltd, said companies firstly needed to involve the Canadian broking community.
"They also need to be sensitive to the fact that one of the new duties of management now is to be out telling (the company's) story," he said at a Securities Institute of Australia address.
"The junior companies which are coming to list are not household names. Outside of the specific investors and people who are close to the company no-one in the world knows them."

The VSE, a niche venture capital exchange that raised more than C$2 billion in 1996, has attracted interest in Australia over the past year because of its perceived willingness to fund blue-sky exploration.

McFadden said 12 companies were listed on both VSE and Australian Stock Exchange (ASX), while another 21 companies listed on the VSE had an Australian association, such as a joint venture or an interest in an Australian mining property.
Five more Australian companies were in the process of listing, and three of these would be listed on both the VSE and ASX.
McFadden said many of the interlisted Australian companies had a project in production providing cash flow, and properties in Asia with blue-sky potential to attract investors.
A review of the 12 interlisted companies found those that raised capital in Canada improved their VSE turnover, he said.
Two saw more turnover on the VSE than on the ASX, but for others, VSE trade could be less than one percent of ASX trade.
All VSE turnover, however, represented additional trading.
McFadden said the total market capitalisation of the 12 was C$300 million, ranging from C$4 million to C$67 million, with an average capitalistion of C$25 million.
Six of these had raised a total of more than C$30 million on the VSE, he said.
McFadden said price performance was mixed.
"Generally the share prices of the companies increased on speculation of their inter-listing on Vancouver and then there was a price decline following the listing," he said.
He also noted that Canadian investors were not comfortable with the Australian practice of a junior miner having having 100 million shares on issue at 10 cents a share.
"We are much more used to having 10 million shares outstanding trading in the C$1.00 range," he said.
